members: Brexanolone (Zulresso): IV infusion 60h, cyclodextrin formulation of natural allopregnanolone (StahlNeuro p.320)
Zuranolone (Zurzuvae): Oral synthetic analogue of allopregnanolone, 14-day course (StahlNeuro p.322)
drug_class.mechanism: Positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) at synaptic and extrasynaptic GABA-A receptors containing delta (δ) subunits (StahlNeuro p.260-262, p.320-322)
kinetics: Brexanolone requires cyclodextrin solubilization for 60h continuous IV (StahlNeuro p.320)
Zuranolone oral absorption requires fat-containing meal (StahlNeuro p.322)
drug_class.onset_of_effect: Rapid onset within 60 hours for Brexanolone and 3 days for Zuranolone (StahlNeuro p.320, p.322)

high_yield: Peripartum onset specifier defined as MDE onset during pregnancy or within first 4 weeks postpartum (DSM p.173, p.213).
Extrasynaptic GABA-A receptors contain delta (δ) subunits, mediate tonic inhibition, are benzodiazepine-insensitive, and are targeted by neuroactive steroids (StahlNeuro p.260-262).
Rapid antidepressant response (60 hours / 3 days) contrasts with 2-8 weeks required for traditional SSRIs/SNRIs (Dulcan p.252; StahlNeuro p.320, p.322).
Treating maternal depression directly improves psychiatric and social outcomes in offspring without child medication (Dulcan p.252; StahlKids p.91, p.201).
Zuranolone oral bioavailability strictly requires co-administration with a fat-containing meal (StahlNeuro p.322).
